title: Bava Batra 6b (3)

chapters.title: Roof adjacent to a courtyard
chapters.about: Hezek Re'iyah rights and wall obligations

chapters.title: Roof to roof privacy
chapters.about: Usage differences between roofs and courtyards

chapters.title: Ri Megas and Harambam on roof usage
chapters.about: Distinguishing between usable and non-usable roofs

claims: "The class also examines cases where properties are at different heights and the resulting obligations for sharing construction costs." - The transcript does not contain this specific discussion; it focuses on roofs and courtyards, but the specific analysis of sharing construction costs for properties at different heights is not presented as a topic in the class.

"He discusses the differing opinions of the Rishonim, including Rashi, Tosafot, Ri Megas, and Harambam, on how to determine when a roof requires a wall for privacy or security." - While the teacher mentions these names, he does not present a comparative analysis of their differing opinions on determining when a roof requires a wall; he mostly discusses their interpretations of the Gemara's specific cases.
summary: Rabbi Harari explores the Gemara in Masechet Bava Batra regarding the responsibilities of neighbors to build walls between adjacent roofs and courtyards. He discusses the differing opinions of the Rishonim, including Rashi, Tosafot, Ri Megas, and Harambam, on how to determine when a roof requires a wall for privacy or security. The class also examines cases where properties are at different heights and the resulting obligations for sharing construction costs.
questions: Do I have to pay for a wall if my neighbor's roof is adjacent to my courtyard?
Why does the Gemara distinguish between the usage of a roof and a courtyard?
If my neighbor's property is at a different height than mine, how do we split the cost of a wall?
What is the purpose of the ten tefahim wall requirement?
Does a roof that is rarely used still require a privacy wall?
